clue.text: Fuel in gallons on sale after moving east

indicators.note: after places the compass point at the tail of what precedes it in the answer

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for gallons

indicators.note: things that are moving shift about, so the letters of the phrase before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A garage advertises fuel sold by the gallon, offered cheaply once the business relocated east.
explanation.walkthrough: GASOLENE is a variant spelling of gasoline, the American word for petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasolene is petrol, the liquid burned in car engines, so it is a type of fuel.

clue.text: The main point of logistics?

indicators.note: of says the letters wanted are taken out from within the word that follows

parts.note: the four letters sitting in the middle of this word

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the central idea of supply-chain management really is.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside logistics, and the question mark admits that it is also, playfully, the central part of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist of something is its essence or core meaning, the central idea a listener should take away.

clue.text: Points out engine part

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic indicates a faulty component inside a motor.
explanation.definitionFit: A piston is the cylinder-shaped component that moves up and down inside an internal combustion motor.

clue.text: Rips hat off a musician

indicators.note: off here suggests something gone wrong or out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone snatches the headgear off a performer's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A harpist plays the harp, the large stringed instrument, and so is one kind of musician.

clue.text: Arrange time for an equestrian event

parts.note: to dress is to arrange, as in dressing a shop window or troops in a line
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone books a slot in the diary to attend a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrange looks like an instruction to shuffle letters, but it is a plain synonym of dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the competitive discipline in which a rider guides a horse through precise trained movements.

clue.text: Fortune-teller and rock star featuring on old record by Queen

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so the letters of the next word are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
O is a common abbreviation for old
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword queen

explanation.surface: A clairvoyant and a rock musician appear together on a vintage album by the band Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Rock star reads as one phrase about music, but rock is the signal to rearrange star, and Queen is not the band but ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrologer claims to predict people's futures from the positions of the planets, a kind of prophet.

clue.text: West Indian close to running one out for a duck

parts.note: WI is the abbreviation for West Indian, as in the cricket team

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of place, so the letters are rearranged
the close of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A West Indian cricketer, while scampering between the wickets, is run out without scoring: a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman out for no runs has made a duck; here the duck is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The wigeon is a dabbling wildfowl species, so it is one particular kind of waterbird in that family.

clue.text: Church built of black American quartz

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
A is a standard abbreviation for American
quartz is crystalline silica, silicon dioxide

explanation.surface: A cathedral constructed from dark stone mined in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica is a large oblong church building, or one granted special status by the Pope.

clue.text: Onion originally included in stir-fried potato dish

indicators.note: included in places one piece inside the other
frying turns things over in the pan, so the letters of the word before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

indicators.note: originally points to the very start, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the vegetable

explanation.surface: A recipe for a fried potato dish with chopped onion mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir-fried reads as one cooking term, but stir supplies letters and fried tells you to mix them. Rosti is a Swiss grated-potato cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosti is a Swiss pancake of grated potato fried until crisp, so it is a dish made from potatoes.

clue.text: Pole position

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an upright stake, as a gatepost
second meaning: a job or station, as an appointment

explanation.walkthrough: Pole position suggests the front of a motor-racing grid, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an upright wooden stake fixed in the ground and a job or assigned station.

clue.text: Records attempts to make wall hangings

parts.note: tapes are recordings, and to tape is to record
tries are attempts

explanation.surface: Someone documents their efforts at producing decorative textiles.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestries are woven pictorial textiles traditionally hung on interior walls for decoration and warmth.

clue.text: Organism spreading disease discovered by a north European

parts.note: a germ is a microbe that causes illness
taken as written
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A microbe carrying an illness is identified by a scientist from northern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: North European looks like one phrase, but north only supplies a letter and the definition is the last word alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A German is a native of Germany, a country in Europe, so one particular European national.

clue.text: Month during which different son and daughter find time to honour parent

indicators.note: during which means the following pieces happen inside the span of the month, so they sit within it

parts.note: May is a month of the year
other means different
S is the abbreviation for son
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: In a certain month the children make time to celebrate one of their parents.
explanation.walkthrough: MOTHERS DAY is the day for honouring mothers; in Britain it falls in March or April, in America in May.
explanation.definitionFit: Mother's Day is an annual occasion set aside for children to celebrate and thank their mums.

clue.text: Bird taking sunfish

parts.note: the first half, sun: the sun is a star
the second half, fish: the ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A bird snatches a sunfish to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunfish is one word in the clue, but it splits into sun and fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The starling is a common speckled songbird known for its huge swirling flocks, called murmurations.

clue.text: Drained wife has heart trouble to face bravely

indicators.note: something drained has been emptied of its contents, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters only

indicators.note: trouble suggests disorder, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An exhausted wife has a cardiac complaint and must be courageous about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart trouble sounds medical, but trouble only tells you to rearrange heart.
explanation.definitionFit: To weather a storm or crisis is to come through it, enduring hardship with courage.

clue.text: Returned fabric, cut and inspected

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the pieces are read from the end to the start

parts.note: denim is a cotton twill fabric used for jeans
to axe is to cut, as in budget cuts

explanation.surface: Cloth sent back to a shop was trimmed and then checked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something is to look at it closely and carefully, the same as inspecting it.

clue.text: Has to accept the limitations of giving to people asking for money

definitions.text: Has to accept the limitations of giving
definitions.note: a cryptic description of the people, from the proverb, rather than a verb
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the proverb says these people cannot be choosers, so they must take what they are given
second meaning: people who solicit charity in the street

explanation.walkthrough: The first part alludes to the saying 'beggars can't be choosers': those who rely on gifts must accept whatever is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: Beggars are people who ask strangers for coins or food, living on charity rather than earnings.

clue.text: Plant needing two women

parts.note: Rose is a woman's name
Mary is another woman's name

explanation.surface: A gardener says some plant needs two women to look after it.
explanation.walkthrough: Two women supplies two separate girls' names placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic evergreen shrub whose needle-like leaves are used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Beautiful girl dropping drug in setter's cocktail

indicators.note: dropping means letting something fall away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman, as the belle of the ball
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
taken as written
the setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A pretty woman slips something into the compiler's drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Setter's reads as possessive, but it stands for setter is, the setter writing as I.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bellini is a cocktail of prosecco and peach purée, first mixed at Harry's Bar in Venice.

clue.text: Olive spread developed a deep tan

indicators.note: developed means turned into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with olive skin spread out in the sun and got a dark suntan.
explanation.walkthrough: Olive spread suggests a sunbather's complexion, but it is a Provençal paste.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapenade is a Provençal paste of chopped olives, capers and anchovies, eaten spread on bread.

clue.text: Get one's own back with a volume on gene mutation

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: a mutation is a change in genetic material, so the letters of the word before it change their order

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for volume
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist takes revenge by publishing a book about genetic mutation.
explanation.walkthrough: Gene mutation reads as biology, but mutation is the signal to rearrange gene.
explanation.definitionFit: To avenge a wrong is to take revenge for it, paying someone back for harm done.

clue.text: Pressure bandage applied round top of ulcer

indicators.note: round places the first piece so that it encloses the second

parts.note: to dress a wound is to bandage it

indicators.note: in a down-style reading the top is the first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A compression bandage is put on around the head of a sore.
explanation.walkthrough: Pressure bandage reads as one medical item, but pressure is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Duress is compulsion by threats or force, pressure put on someone to act against their will.

clue.text: Map discovered by soldiers going back into cave

indicators.note: into places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a den is a cave or lair

indicators.note: going back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A treasure map is found by troops retreating into a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: To map out something is to plan or lay it out, which is what to design means as a verb.

clue.text: Sections of poem about a sick French city

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes around the rest

parts.note: verses are the stanzas or lines of a poem
taken as written
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Some stanzas of a poem describe an ailing city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Versailles is a city west of Paris, famous for the royal palace built by Louis XIV.

clue.text: Beast next to end of steep slope

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, an animal

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An animal stands at the bottom of a steep hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is an inclined surface joining two levels, a sloping walkway or roadway.

clue.text: Vermin running around two state capitals

indicators.note: capitals are the capital letters, the initial letters of the preceding words

parts.note: the first letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Pests scurry about between two state capital cities.
explanation.walkthrough: State capitals suggests cities such as Albany, but capitals means initial letters of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats are rodents regarded as pests that spread disease and spoil food, classic examples of vermin.

clue.text: Foreign lager gets a disapproving look

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker ordering imported beer is frowned upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A glare is a fierce angry stare, a hostile expression of disapproval directed at someone.

clue.text: Useless to turn weapon on a politician

indicators.note: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon
taken as written
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: It is pointless to aim a gun at a member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Nugatory means of no value or effect, futile, so something nugatory is worthless and pointless.
